findings.evidence: `grep '^theorem' TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/Dissipative/Basic.lean` gives `IsDissipative.norm_le_of_smul_sub_eq`, `IsDissipative.smul_sub_injective`, `IsMDissipative.smul_sub_surjective`, `IsMDissipative.smul_sub_bijective`, `IsMDissipative.mem_resolventSet`, `IsMDissipative.norm_resolvent_le` — all `hA`-first lemmas are namespaced. The new lemma's immediate sibling `IsMDissipative.norm_resolvent_le` (Dissipative/Basic.lean:348) proves the unscaled form of the same bound.
findings.fix: Rename to `IsMDissipative.norm_smul_resolvent_le_one` (and call it as `hA.norm_smul_resolvent_le_one hlambda` at lines 97 and 176).
findings.issue: `norm_smul_resolvent_le_one` has no Yosida content — it is purely the statement that `lambda • R(lambda, A)` is a contraction for m-dissipative `A` — yet it sits bare in `TauCeti.Semigroups` while taking `hA : IsMDissipative A` as its first explicit argument. Every other lemma of this shape in the repo is in the `IsMDissipative` namespace, so dot notation works there and not here.

findings.evidence: Yosida.lean:140 states `‖exp (t • yosidaApproximation A lambda)‖ ≤ 1`; Yosida.lean:79/81 names the `smul` in `norm_smul_resolvent_le_one : ‖lambda • LinearPMap.resolvent A lambda‖ ≤ 1`. Mathlib spells the operand similarly in `hasDerivAt_exp_smul_const` / `differentiable_exp_smul_const` (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Exponential.lean).
findings.issue: `norm_exp_yosidaApproximation_le_one` names the conclusion `‖exp (yosidaApproximation A lambda)‖ ≤ 1`, but the statement is `‖exp (t • yosidaApproximation A lambda)‖ ≤ 1`; the `t •` operand is dropped from the name. The same file spells out `smul` in `norm_smul_resolvent_le_one` for the analogous `‖lambda • R‖ ≤ 1`.

summary: Terminology and most names are standard and consistent with the adjacent resolvent/dissipative API. Two names are off: an m-dissipativity fact placed outside the `IsMDissipative` namespace, and an exponential bound whose name drops the `smul` operand.
